item.title: Active Release-Style Forearm Extensor Technique
clinicalUse: Forearm extensor stiffness/pain where active tissue excursion improves symptoms
contact: Controlled contact over extensor muscle mass.
forceDirection: Maintain pressure while patient moves wrist from shortened toward lengthened position.
steps: 2. Position wrist so tissue is shortened.
safety: Avoid acute tear, hematoma, nerve symptoms.
item.visualCue: Contact maintained + tissue actively lengthens → re-test grip/motion.

subTechniques.name: Common wrist extensors — Active Soft-Tissue Release
subTechniques.clinicalGoal: Improve pain, movement tolerance or tissue-related function when this target is clinically relevant.
subTechniques.patientSetup: Sitting or supine with the upper limb supported.
subTechniques.contact: Tolerable contact over Common wrist extensors while the tissue begins in a shortened position.
subTechniques.direction: Maintain controlled contact while the patient actively lengthens/moves the target tissue.
subTechniques.dosage: Often 3–8 slow repetitions followed by reassessment.
subTechniques.reassess: Re-test the region's original pain, range or functional task.
